signature_type.name: ethereum
signature_type.algorithm: secp256k1 ECDSA, RFC 6979 nonces, low s, v in {27, 28}
signature_type.signed_message: EIP-191 personal_sign over the RAW 48-byte deep hash: keccak256("\x19Ethereum Signed Message:\n48" || deep hash)

key_rule: private key = SHA-256(UTF-8("turbo-upload type 3 corpus/" + name)); public key and address by ethers
connect_message: sign this message to connect to your account
notes: Every byte under `expected`, signature and id included, must match exactly.
Each item was signed twice, by EthereumSigner (key) and InjectedEthereumSigner (wallet), with identical bytes.
`wallet_path` is what the wallet signed to reveal its public key, before the first item.
No private key is stored: each one is derived from its case name by the key rule.

vectors.name: empty-data-empty-tags
vectors.description: The degenerate item: no data, no tags, no target, no anchor. Pins the 1044-byte floor of the format and proves absent optional fields still contribute a zero-length blob to the deep hash.

vectors.name: ascii-data-no-tags
vectors.description: Small ASCII payload, no tags. The simplest non-trivial item; the tag region is 16 bytes of zeroed counters and nothing else.

vectors.name: single-byte-data
vectors.description: One data byte. Catches implementations that special-case or off-by-one the data offset.

vectors.name: one-tag
vectors.description: A single Content-Type tag. Pins the minimal Avro tag block: zigzag count, one name/value pair, terminating 0x00.

vectors.name: several-tags
vectors.description: Five tags in declared order. Tag order is significant and is never sorted or normalised.

vectors.name: duplicate-tag-names
vectors.description: The same tag name three times with different values. ANS-104 does not require unique names and no deduplication happens; all three survive in order.

vectors.name: unicode-tags
vectors.description: Non-ASCII in both tag names and values: Latin-1 accents, CJK, Cyrillic, and an astral-plane emoji (surrogate pair). The declared varint length is the UTF-8 BYTE length, not the character or UTF-16 code-unit count, this is where naive encoders break.

vectors.name: empty-tag-value
vectors.description: A tag with a non-empty name and an empty value. The value serializes as a zero-length string: varint 0x00 and no bytes.

vectors.name: empty-tag-name
vectors.description: A tag with an EMPTY NAME. arbundles permits this and round-trips it; ANS-104 does not forbid it. A validator that rejects empty names diverges from the de-facto reference.

vectors.name: empty-name-and-value
vectors.description: Both name and value empty. Four bytes of tag region: count, 0x00, 0x00, terminator.

vectors.name: tag-value-64-bytes
vectors.description: A well-formed UTF-8 tag value of exactly 64 bytes, the last length that takes arbundles' hand-rolled encoder path. Must byte-match the 65-byte case's encoder.

vectors.name: tag-value-65-bytes
vectors.description: The same content plus one byte, which crosses arbundles' internal 64-byte threshold and switches it to Buffer.write. Both paths must agree for well-formed input; this vector is the guard on that.

vectors.name: lone-surrogate-tag-short
vectors.description: KNOWN DIVERGENCE. An unpaired UTF-16 high surrogate (U+D800) in a tag value under 64 bytes. arbundles' hand-rolled encoder emits the raw code point as WTF-8 (ED A0 80) while declaring Buffer.byteLength (3), which is the length of the standard-UTF-8 replacement character. Standard UTF-8 would emit EF BF BD. Same width, different bytes, so nothing desyncs and nothing errors, a reimplementation just silently produces a different id.

vectors.name: lone-surrogate-tag-long
vectors.description: KNOWN DIVERGENCE, other side. The same unpaired surrogate in a value over 64 bytes, where arbundles falls through to Buffer.write and emits standard UTF-8 (EF BF BD). Identical logical input to the previous vector, different bytes, purely because of length. arbundles is not self-consistent here.

vectors.name: binary-data-all-bytes
vectors.description: Data is all 256 byte values 0x00..0xFF, not valid UTF-8. Data is an opaque byte string and must never be routed through a text codec.

vectors.name: data-4096-bytes
vectors.description: Exactly 4096 bytes of data. A size boundary that shares its number with MAX_TAG_BYTES, which is a common place to conflate two unrelated limits.

vectors.name: target-present
vectors.description: Target present, anchor absent. Flips the target presence byte to 1 and inserts 32 bytes, shifting every subsequent offset by 32.

vectors.name: anchor-present
vectors.description: Anchor present, target absent. NOTE arbundles takes the anchor argument as a raw string and Buffer.from()s it, the anchor is 32 RAW BYTES, not a base64url-decoded value the way target is. Passing a 43-char base64url anchor throws.

vectors.name: target-and-anchor
vectors.description: Both optional fields present, no tags. The layout with the maximum optional-field displacement.

vectors.name: everything-present
vectors.description: Target, anchor, several unicode tags and a non-empty payload all at once. The integration case: if offsets are computed independently anywhere, this is where it shows.

vectors.name: max-tag-set
vectors.description: 90 tags, filling the tag region to just under the 4096-byte MAX_TAG_BYTES cap. Also crosses the 63-tag boundary where the zigzag varint for the tag count grows to two bytes.

vectors.name: tag-count-varint-boundary
vectors.description: Exactly 64 tags. Zigzag(64) = 128, the first count that needs a two-byte varint (0x80 0x01). A single-byte-varint assumption dies here.
